The 18 conformers of the Ag complex sorted by the signs of two dihedrals around the Ag–C4 bond.

**Files used** (from the repository):

* `files/ensemble.xyz` — 18 conformers of an Ag complex, 168 atoms (comment line = energy)

**1. One dihedral**, P50–Ag0–C4–N3.

```bash
frog-sort files/ensemble.xyz -i 50 0 4 3
```

```text
…
╰──────┴──────────────┴──────────╯
     Categories
(files/ensemble.xyz)
╭──────────┬───────╮
│ Category │ Count │
├──────────┼───────┤
│ N        │    10 │
│ P        │     8 │
╰──────────┴───────╯
```

Only the end of the output is shown: 10 conformers have a negative dihedral (N) and 8 a positive one (P).

**2. Two dihedrals, and write one file per category.**

```bash
frog-sort files/ensemble.xyz -i 50 0 4 3 -i 83 0 4 3 -w --out-dir sorted
```

`sorted/ensemble_PN.xyz` (first 3 lines):

```text
168
-257.39917162
Ag    -0.510426     0.206915     0.006150
…
```

* Three codes out of four possible: NP (10 conformers), PP (5) and PN (3). NN does not occur and no
  file is written for it.
* The second dihedral (83-0-4-3) is always far from 0° (112.49° to 174.99°, or −173.32° to −164.52°).
  It changes sign only for conformers 14–16, where it is close to 180°, so the PP/PN split is not
  chemically meaningful. The first dihedral is the one that separates the two families.
* `sorted/ensemble_PN.xyz` keeps the CREST energy as comment line (−257.39917162).
